newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean groups plan corn shipment to North Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean groups plan corn shipment to North Korea.

text.p: Religious and other civic groups in South Korea plan to raise about $20 million to ship 110,000 tonnes of corn to hunger-stricken North Korea, their spokesman said on Tuesday.

"We have already raised 1.37 billion won ($1.53 million) and set a target of raising 17 billion won ($18.99 million) over the next two months," said Kim Sung-yeoun, planning manager at the Korea Sharing Movement.

Kim said the groups plan to ship 5,000 tonnes of corn to North Korea next week and another 5,000 tonnes the following week with the money they had raised. The shipments will be made through the South Korean Red Cross.

Six major religious groups and 22 civic organisations initially wanted to raise 1.7 billion won in the 11 days that ended on Monday to cover the estimated cost of sending 10,000 tonnes of corn to the impoverished North, he said.
"Luckily corn prices are softer than we earlier thought and we can go ahead with our plan to ship 10,000 tonnes of corn to North Korea," he said.
The targeted 17 billion won was expected to cover the cost of a further 100,000 tonnes of corn, to give a total of 110,000 tonnes.

Kim said the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) and other international aid groups had warned that famine could strike North Korea in the near future, and the South Korean groups decided to share some food with "our brethren in the North".
"Our target is a daunting one but we are confident we will meet it," he said. "Our campaign is picking up pace."

Last week, the South Korean Red Cross sent more than $1 million worth of food and vegetable seed to North Korea, the largest food delivery by the organisation since such shipments began in November 1995.
Separately last week, the Seoul government lifted a ban on private organisations providing rice to Pyongyang and allowed local business groups to join food aid programmes for the North.
Previously, only local religious and civic groups and individual South Koreans could ship non-rice food aid to the North. Seoul had maintained rice could be diverted to the military.
The United Nations on Monday launched an appeal for $126.2 million for North Korea to stave off famine. Of the funds, $95 million are for food supplies announced last week by the WFP.
The Seoul government has also made several goodwill gestures recently in an apparent bid to lure the North to proposed peace talks among the two Koreas, China and the United States.
The talks, jointly proposed by the United States and South Korea a year earlier, are aimed at securing a peace treaty to replace a truce that ended the 1950-53 Korean War.
U.S. officials said on Monday North Korea had told Washington it would soon decide whether to join the peace talks.

One official said Washington believed Pyongyang had been positively influenced by the "cumulative affect" of recent food aid appeals for North Korea and was optismistic the Stalinist regime would agree to join the talks.
The WFP has said North Korea faces a grain shortage of 2.3 million tonnes this year.
